en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī-mantra of King Adornment, Spoken by the Buddha. One fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing by Imperial Command.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was on Mount Potalaka for the sake of all...
To the entire great assembly of humans and devas, he expounded the essential points of the Dharma.
Surveying the ten directions with his wondrous voice,
he addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
"Noble son, there is a sūtra titled 'The Dhāraṇī of the King Who Protects and Observes All Sentient Beings and Manifests the Adornments of Buddha-fields of All Tathāgatas.
When I first resolved to attain enlightenment in the past,"
In the presence of the Tathāgata Flower-Light Manifestation,
ninety koṭis of sentient beings,
upon hearing this Dharma but once, all attained a portion of the Tathāgata’s wisdom and were each granted a prophecy of enlightenment.
"You shall attain Buddhahood in various Buddha-fields;
I too have received the prediction of enlightenment therein from the Buddha.
Son of good family, with my Buddha-eye..."
He beheld thirty thousand Tathāgatas of the past who,
for the sake of all sentient beings, expounded this essential Dharma.
You, Avalokiteśvara and Mañjuśrī—
At the time of preaching the Dharma, they all served as leaders. Then,
after the World-Honored One had spoken these words,
the great assembly present— the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and all who had come to listen— [were moved].
All of them gave rise to faith and made offerings to that Buddha.

At that time, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings all received predictions of their future enlightenment and also attained the sublime and wondrous samādhis of bodhisattvas.
All sufferings of illness shall be eliminated, and all obscurations and entanglements shall be extinguished.
One's aspirations will be fulfilled, roots of goodness will be perfected,
one’s countenance will become upright and handsome, and wealth and treasures will abound.
Kings, ministers, and all classes of sentient beings who saw him were filled with joy.
His mindfulness, wisdom, and supernormal powers were perfectly complete;
he attained indestructible faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha.
They possess longevity, physical strength, and great majestic power;
they are free from the suffering of being separated from what is loved and encountering what is hated.
If there are sons or daughters of good family, and so forth, [who...]
Those who are able to prostrate with their five limbs touching the ground toward this sutra and give rise to a sense of rare wonder,
and who respectfully make offerings of various flowers, incense, garlands, banners, and canopies,
taking refuge in it, praising it, reading and reciting it, and upholding it;
Whether one writes it oneself or instructs others to write it,
immeasurable merits will all be fully accomplished;
upon seeing those who receive and uphold it, one should give rise to a mind of faith and reverence.
Furthermore, in this very life, they will be endowed with all virtues and attain the supreme, wondrous samādhis of a bodhisattva;
from their mouths, the fragrance of sandalwood will constantly issue forth.
Their eyes were bright and pure like the petals of a blue lotus.
Throughout the day and night, they beheld the forms of the Buddha and the great bodhisattvas.
As for those who possessed the karmic obstructions of the five sins of immediate retribution and other such offenses, [they were all purified].
All [obstacles] shall be completely extinguished, and they will be protected by the devas.
At the time of death, they shall behold the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with an undisturbed mind and will certainly attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
I have bestowed the prediction of buddhahood upon these people;
seeing my body, they pay respectful homage and harbor no doubt regarding the mind of sublime enlightenment.
Furthermore, if there should be anyone who reads,
recites, receives, upholds, makes offerings to, and honors this Dharma-gate,
whether writing it themselves or instructing others to write it;
Furthermore, one who hears the name of this sutra should be known as a bodhisattva worthy of being honored and served.
Yet, if such a person, due to prior evil karma...
Wealth, life-span, physical appearance, and strength— all internal and external resources— are entirely deficient;
their desires remain unfulfilled, they suffer separation from loved ones,
and their lands become desolate and ruined due to the calamities of kings and bandits.
By the power of this sutra, one experiences lightness of body in the present life;
or perhaps suffers a temporary headache, obtains coarse clothing and poor food,
or encounters verbal abuse and other forms of humiliation.
All past karmic obstructions will be spontaneously eliminated.
Good son, that person who upholds this sutra should give rise to this thought:
"In the past, I wandered within the ocean of birth and death."
Having committed various evils against sentient beings,
my unwholesome karma has increased day and night;
now, having become awakened to this, I dare not conceal it.
Revealing the source of one's offenses and sincerely repenting,
one should give rise to indestructible faith in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha.
Furthermore, if that person...
If one has committed various evil deeds against the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, or against pratyekabuddhas, śrāvakas, parents, teachers, or elders,
the karmic retribution for food and clothing will all be exhausted;
yet, by the power of this sutra, all such karma is entirely eliminated, and food and clothing become abundant.
Furthermore, if that person has karma for suffering in the hells,
karma for the suffering of separation from loved ones, or karma for the maturation of being born blind,
lacking sense organs, or having two sexual organs— all such karmas shall likewise be extinguished.
Furthermore, due to the power of previous karma consisting of envy, malice, and hatred,
one would otherwise fall into the realms of King Yama, among the animals, hungry ghosts,
and other evil destinies; however, by the power of this sutra, all such evil karma will be extinguished without exception.
All merits and virtues will increase.
Son of good family, in whatever place this Dharma-gate exists,
those people shall always be protected by this sutra.
Endowed with merit, their aspirations will be fulfilled;
they shall constantly enjoy wealth and happiness, and their evil karma will be eliminated.
Furthermore, they shall suffer no untimely death nor any evil dreams.
They shall be free from the suffering of illness, always victorious in battle, and enjoy an extended lifespan.
Endowed with physical strength and vigor, they shall possess great majesty;
all people of the world, as well as devas, nāgas, and various spirits, shall all follow their will.
They shall not encounter the calamities of evil poisons, water, fire,
or untimely misfortunes; moreover, by the power of upholding this divine mantra,
they shall always receive the prophetic assurance (*vyākaraṇa*) from all the Buddhas.
If good sons or good daughters hear such a divine mantra,
receive and uphold it, read and recite it,
or write it themselves or instruct others to write it, and honor and make offerings to it.
Those sons and daughters of good family shall all obtain the merits previously described.
When the World-Honored One had spoken these words, [the assembly rejoiced].
Suddenly, the great earth shook in six ways.
This great assembly [honored him] with exquisite flowers,
incense, unguents, garlands, canopies, and superior, wonderful robes.
They offered this to the World-Honored One, chanting in unison:
"Excellent, excellent!
How may we hear the divine mantra spoken by the Tathāgata?"
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
*Namo sarva-tathāgatānām | tadyathā | bṛte | subṛte | lokavilokite | lokavidhikaraṇī | sattvāvaloke* ||1||
Kaṇi (7) sarvathāgatādhiṣṭhite (8) sarvāśāparipūrṇe (9) jundare (10) narendrabhūṣite (11) tathāgatajñānadarśane (12) tathāgatādhiṣṭhāna.
Nirna 13. Sarvaloka-sukhi-bhavatu 14. Sarvakarmapariśodhanāya 15. Mama amuka-nāmā 16.
Sarvasattvānām 17. Rakṣa bhavatu 18. Tathāgatādhiṣṭhānam.
*ṣṭhānide* (19) *svāhā* (20). Any syllables formed at the edge of the mouth may be pronounced with the tongue rolled back (*ūṣman*).
O son of good family, this divine mantra—
This has been proclaimed by thirty thousand Tathāgatas and is collectively empowered by them;
I now likewise recite this divine mantra for the benefit of all sentient beings.
May they attain peace and happiness, constantly receiving protection;
may their illnesses and sufferings be eliminated, and may they be born in the lands of the Buddhas.
Furthermore, if there are those who conceive such a thought:
"Regarding the merits of the divine mantra as spoken by the Buddha,
how can I now achieve them? Thinking thus,
he rose early in the morning and purified himself.
Extending great compassion toward all sentient beings and giving rise to a mind of pity,
one should eliminate all envy, pride, and malice,
and with a respectful and single-minded heart, stand before an image of the Buddha.
Extensively offer incense, flowers, food, and drink as offerings;
prostrate to the Buddhas of the ten directions and pray for your aspirations with all your heart;
then recite this divine mantra one hundred and eight times.
For each of the directions, one should consecrate a flower with the mantra once;
by offering each flower to the Buddha,
this person shall immediately obtain whatever they seek according to their aspirations.
Everything shall be fulfilled according to their wishes.
They shall also behold the Buddhas within their dreams,
and at the time of death, they shall see the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
After casting off this body, one will certainly attain rebirth in the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
There, one’s lifespan, physical form, and strength will all be fully perfected,
and all enemies and adversaries will give rise to joy.
When this mantra was spoken, sixty thousand sentient beings attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
All obstacles were forever eliminated, and their aspirations were fulfilled.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having finished speaking this sutra, [entered into meditative absorption].
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
along with the entire great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
Thus ends the *Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī-Mantra of King Adornment* as spoken by the Buddha.
